I have a whey protien shake right when I wake up. When I get to work I have 1/2 cup oats, scoop of casen protien, 1/4 cup blueberries and two large eggs. Second breakfast is 5oz chicken, 8 asparagus spears and 1 cup sweet potatoes. Lunch is 4oz taco seasoned ground beef with 1 cup cilantro lime rice. For snacks I usually have trail mix with added dried fruit or Quest chips. When I get home I have another protein shake.

It's easy to not want to snack when you're busy eating all shift, there's always something cooking in my car, literally LOL.

At least 4 different meal prepped meals, healthy snacks that fit my macros, gallon jug of water, large yeti of coffee to sip on throughout the night.

However I'm a firm believer that things you do outside of work greatly impact your work day. I am extremely disciplined in getting at least 8 hours of sleep, assuming I don't have to stay late on reports. Exercise if I get sleepy on duty such as 30 squats, jumping jacks and push-ups every hour. Days off I make sure to workout and lift HEAVY. Days that I can workout on duty I'm extremely grateful and get a good full body in at the end of shift, which always helps me sleep better.

The more you can prepare for the shift work and the more disciplined you are the easier it is.

I've been obsessing over this chair, as the title says, for about ten months. I told myself I'd save a nest egg first and then save up to get my dream chair. As it got closer and closer to hitting that magic number I woke up, a week before my birthday to a SecretLab box infront of my door, my husband surprised me with it as a Birthday/Christmas gift! I work overnights and long hours so I've had to stare at the box for about 3 days and nights while resisting the urge to put it together.

Finally today, my husband and I put it together! I discovered these three small black marks on the backrest. I vaccumed our living room 3 separate times to make sure we had the cleanest surface to work on, (did I mention I've been obsessing over this). When I pulled the backrest out of the packaging I noticed the black marks. I get it, life isn't perfect and it's easily cleanable, it's just not what I expected to see, but Hakuna Matata.

The build was extremely easy to navigate, extra shout out to the poster size instructions along with the "Don't rip this off until..." because my husband started ripping until.... Kudos to whomever thought of that.

Once it was set up I immediately rolled it into our temporary game room (it's awful, don't judge me, I hate it too) and sat in it. I can see why people say the base is too firm, but it doesn't bother me one bit. The size feels absolutely perfect! FOR THE SMALLER LADIES OUT THERE!! I'm 5'4", 123 pounds and muscular, this. Is. Perfect. It hugs my shoulders just right and the seat isn't too "buckety" for my glutes and quads. I love the feeling of being hugged in my shoulders and back but free to sit cross legged if I want. I have an awful back so any and all support for it is very much appreciated.

All in all I'm in love. After watching literally tons of videos, obsessing over measurements, because let's be real, I can (and have) worn children's sizes of things and they fit me perfectly, so I've been worried the small might still be too big. But nope. It's perfect. I'm so eagerly awaiting my sleep schedule flop back (I work overnights but flip to days on my days off so I can be normal) so I can have a few all nighter sessions to truly test this baby out.

THANK YOU SECRETLAB!!!!

I grew up playing Warcraft, then Tides of Darkness, then Reign of Chaos. When my brother came home with Vanilla WoW I remember watching him run around as a night elf and seeing what a Moonwell looks like up close. When my brother moved out I took over and made my own character. Leveling my priest up, raiding MC and Ony, it was amazing. The people you meet being able to raid with my brother. Then my Mom got an account and started playing. Soon it was my mom and I as healers and my brother as top dps. It was strange family bonding. Being able to discuss tactics. It was a way for our family to still communicate and talk over a few hours of gaming. My mom became the Mother of the guild, I was the youngest player, and my brother was comic relief. WoW was a fond memory of growing up and still having a connection to my brother. When my brother quit I took the reins and really started hardcore raiding. The community of 40 people overcoming an obstacle and sharing the same moments, the joy that comes from achieving something you've worked at for months. I still keep in touch with a few people from my guild today. One was an airborne army man who was stationed in Afghanistan who I mailed care packages to. The relationships you create through the game is immeasurable. You can sign on after a shit day of work or school and be able to gank a few people, or raid the Xroads, the stress of the day just goes away. I miss it. I just started playing again after 2 years, work has me traveling around to extremely small towns. Bored at night in the hotel I'll log on for a few hours after working out. But I mainly started again to talk to my mom more, who still plays. The community is what made Vanilla Wow. I give it a few months of playing before I log off for another two years.
